newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmiri industry seeks incentives to revive area.
newsitem.headline: Kashmiri industry seeks incentives to revive area.

text.p: Industrialists in India's troubled state of Jammu and Kashmir said on Sunday they needed liberal policy incentives to put state's ailing economy back on tracks.

"We need to establish a long term industrial programme for rebuilding the state and give new incentives to increase research and development to accelerate output," said Satish Kaul, president of Bari Brahmna Industrial Organisation.
Bari Brahamna, the state's industrial hub, is located 18 kms (11 miles) south of the state's winter capital Jammu.
The industry has suffered a loss of more than 3.0 billion rupees ($83.80 million) during the last seven years due to ongoing insurgency in the state, Kaul said.
"The prevailing militancy has adversely affected the industrial sector and even the payments due from government departments are held up due to non-availablity of funds," Kaul said.
State's economy has slipped dramatically since 1990 when an armed rebellion broke out. More than 20,000 people have been killed in the region disputed by Pakistan.
India and Pakistan have fought two wars over Kashmir since independence from Britain in 1947.
India controls two thirds of the region and accuses Pakistan of supporting an armed rebellion in the state. Pakistan, which controls the remaining third, denies the charges.
"To enable to survive the onslaught of militancy, interest on term loan and capital should be waived," Kaul said.
He emphasised the need for a rational industrial policy. "We have an industrial policy in the shape of subsidy but the execution of policy has not always been encouraging," he said.
"To put all these programmes into practice the government needs to set up a critical industrial commission," he said.
Kaul said improvement of the basic infrastructure in the state, reduction in interest rates, revival of sick units were some of the areas that needed government's immediate attention.

State Industry Minister Bodhraj Bali told Reuters that he has constituted a 22-member industrial advisory committee to look into the problems of entrepreneurs in the state and work out measures for formulating new industrial policy.
"We want to make this state a shining example of industrial power," Bali said.
